images.title: A square has five family names
images.purpose: Shows one square surrounded by the five family names it belongs to.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large square in the centre with five short name tags placed around it, each joined to it by a thin line.
images.exact_structure: One square in dark outline, lightly filled reddish purple (#CC79A7), sitting flat in the centre. Each side carries one identical short tick mark, each corner a small dark square right angle mark, and the top and bottom sides one identical arrowhead each, the left and right sides two identical arrowheads each. Around it, five rounded rectangular name tags with teal (#0072B2) outlines, evenly spaced: Rectangle at the top left, Rhombus at the top right, Parallelogram at the right, Trapezium at the bottom, Kite at the left. A thin grey (#6B7280) line joins each tag to the square. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A square meets every family's definition, so it is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite.
images.description: Shows one square surrounded by the five family names it belongs to.
images.context: All angles 90° (rectangle), all sides equal (rhombus), opposite sides parallel (parallelogram, trapezium), two pairs of equal neighbouring sides (kite).

image_decisions.why: One figure with all its family names shows that a quadrilateral can belong to several families at once.
